title: Cockpit Side Window Frame — Cleat Replacement and Shear Tie Repair

ata.title: Flight Compartment Windows — Side Window Assembly

abstract: Replacement of a cracked or corroded cleat in the cockpit side window frame and repair of the adjacent shear tie, applied with the sliding window removed and the internal trim stripped.

sections.purpose: This repair renews a cracked or corroded cleat in the cockpit side window frame and restores the adjacent shear tie, so that the frame retains its shear capability around the sliding window aperture.
sections.damage_assessment: The frame can only be assessed with the sliding window removed and the internal trim stripped. Inspect every cleat around the aperture by detailed visual and confirm any suspected crack by dye penetrant. Record the cleat position by its clock reference around the aperture. A single cracked cleat may be renewed by this repair. Two or more cracked cleats on the same aperture, a crack that has propagated into the frame web, or corrosion at the shear tie deeper than 10 per cent of its thickness, is outside scope and requires an engineering assessment before the window is refitted.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the sliding window and strip the internal trim from the aperture. Remove the affected cleat by drilling out its fasteners, taking care not to enlarge the holes in the frame. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the exposed frame land and of the shear tie ARD526698-54, and confirm that no indication remains. Where the shear tie shows light corrosion, blend it out inside the limit and measure the remaining thickness. Apply the chromate-free surface protection to all bare metal. Fit the new cleat D5610125021948 dry and check the fit at all three flanges; where the gap exceeds the limit, make a machined shim rather than stacking laminates. Install the cleat wet with sealant using the swaged collars AES234378-94 to the pattern on repair drawing RD-56-10-12-907. Refit the lower clip FJDE819380-76 with the edging grommet AES367595-6E where the harness passes. Refit the sliding window, check the operation through the full travel and do a cabin pressurisation leak check at the aperture.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is not life limited but carries a repeat detailed visual inspection of the renewed cleat and of the adjacent cleats at every C check, and a dye penetrant inspection of the same cleats every 10000 flight hours. Sealant lifting at the cleat flange, or any difficulty in operating the sliding window, is a reason to re-inspect immediately. Report the repair with the cleat clock position so that it is recorded against the aircraft.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: One cracked or corroded cleat per aperture, with no propagation into the frame web and with shear tie corrosion not deeper than 10 per cent of the tie thickness.
